notes.purpose: The reference dialect. It is what examples/sql-php.php proves end to end and what the functional suite runs first, so it is authored before its sibling rather than derived from it.
notes.version: 10.5 is the minimum this document assumes, and it is what every `since` is compared against — not the server actually on the other end of the connection, which a static translator never sees. A deployment on something newer that wants entries gated above 10.5 registers a derived dialect: Map::defineDialect('mariadb-11.8', ['extends' => 'mariadb', 'version' => '11.8']). Being conservative by default is the right way round: refusing a rule that would have worked costs a fallback to the evaluator, while accepting one that will not costs a query that fails at run time.
notes.no-overrides: This leaf overrides nothing any more. RMATCH was its one entry and moved to mysql-family once MySQL 8.4 confirmed the same template, which is what the family layer is for. A leaf that declares only a version is not an empty file: `version` is what every `since` is compared against, and `target: true` is what makes the name usable in translate().
